title: Eating Natto Linked to Better Brain Health
paragraphs: Natto, a traditional Japanese food made from fermented soybeans, is famous for its strong smell and sticky texture. While not everyone enjoys it, a new study from Japan suggests that eating natto regularly may be linked to better brain health in older people.

The study was published in the journal Nutrition Research in 2026. It used data from the Tarumizu Cohort Study, which looks at the health of adults aged 65 and older in Tarumizu, a city in Kagoshima Prefecture in southern Japan. According to reports, the research was carried out by Kagoshima University together with Mizkan, one of Japan's largest natto makers.

The researchers found that older adults who ate natto regularly were less likely to have mild cognitive impairment, a condition in which people have problems with memory or thinking that are more serious than normal for their age. Even after the researchers took other factors into account, regular natto eaters had a significantly lower chance of having this condition. In addition, people who ate natto regularly were less likely to have symptoms of depression.

Other research has found similar results. A large study in Japan, published in 2022, followed about 41,000 adults. It found that eating natto may be linked to a lower risk of serious dementia in women, especially those under 60, although the result was not very strong. Meanwhile, a 2025 analysis of several studies suggested that eating more natto was linked to a lower risk of major cognitive problems.

Natto contains several substances that are produced during fermentation, such as vitamin K2 and an enzyme called nattokinase. Some scientists believe these may be good for health, but most of the evidence comes from studies on animals.

It is important to note that the new study was cross-sectional, which means it looked at people at one point in time. As a result, it cannot prove that eating natto protects the brain. In addition, the study was partly carried out by a company that sells natto.
